description: Official EquiMind Tool Metadata Structure for Database

category.description: Must match one of the 14 existing categories exactly

instructions.description: Complete step-by-step instructions for using the tool (can be multi-paragraph)
instructions.example: This DBT skill helps you pause and regain safety when distress spikes. 1) STOP: Physically freeze...

duration_minutes.description: How long the exercise takes in minutes

description.description: Brief one-sentence summary of the tool
description.example: A pause-and-reset tool to interrupt emotional escalation and regain cognitive clarity.

anxiety_level.description: Which anxiety levels (1-10) this tool is suitable for

confidence_level.description: Which confidence levels (1-10) this tool is suitable for

evidence_base.description: Research backing or clinical approach this tool is based on
evidence_base.example: DBT distress tolerance skills, Sports psychology, HRV research

suitable_for.description: Tags for what conditions/situations this tool addresses

complete_example.name: The 3-Minute Halt (DBT STOP Skill)
complete_example.description: A pause-and-reset tool to interrupt emotional escalation and regain cognitive clarity before making riding decisions.
complete_example.instructions: This DBT skill helps you pause and regain safety when distress spikes. 1) STOP: Physically freeze. Do not react. Take your hands off the reins if needed. 2) TAKE A BREATH: Slow, deep breath in through your nose for 4 counts, out for 6 counts. Repeat 2-3 times. 3) OBSERVE: Notice what you feel in your body (tight chest, shaky hands), what you are thinking (I can't do this, my horse is going to bolt), and what the situation actually is (my horse shifted weight, I heard a loud noise). 4) PROCEED MINDFULLY: Ask yourself: What is the wise choice right now? Options: dismount and walk, do simple circles at the walk, take a break, or end the ride early. Choose the safest, most grounded action.
complete_example.evidence_base: DBT distress tolerance module, Crisis intervention research

notes: The 'id' field should be unique across all tools
Instructions can be as long as needed - use numbered steps for clarity
New metadata fields like 'rider_range', 'horse_range', 'clusters', 'priority' are NOT currently in the database
If you want to add new fields, we can extend the schema, but current tools use the fields listed above
